    <title>Scalable Neural Network Training over Distributed Graphs</title>
    <updated>2024-02-11T08:52:32Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13053v3" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.13053v3" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Graph neural networks (GNNs) fuel diverse machine learning tasks involving graph-structured data, ranging from predicting protein structures to serving personalized recommendations. Real-world graph data must often be stored distributed across many machines not just because of capacity constraints, but because of compliance with data residency or privacy laws. In such setups, network communication is costly and becomes the main bottleneck to train GNNs. Optimizations for distributed GNN training have targeted data-level improvements so far -- via caching, network-aware partitioning, and sub-sampling -- that work for data center-like setups where graph data is accessible to a single entity and data transfer costs are ignored.
